junctions.name: CVG airport trunk / Middle Ring (Hebron)
junctions.note: System and service in one junction. The Middle Ring stays in its cut, 7.1 m under the airport trunk. Every ramp runs at ring level or street level, nothing is built above the ground, and every level change runs beside the ring. Airport traffic never stops. Ring east to the airport leaves the ring east of the trunk, passes under the local road at ring level, climbs beside the ring and turns back over it on a hairpin bridge west of the trunk, then an S-curve and a run beside the trunk before it joins southbound as a new lane. Airport to ring west leaves the trunk northbound well south of the ring on an S-curve, turns over the ring on a hairpin bridge east of the trunk and descends beside the ring under the local road. Ring west to the airport and airport to ring east pass under the hairpins at ring level. Trunk lanes, all continuous: from the signal south over the ring the local road is 2 lanes each way; southbound each airport ramp adds a lane, 4 into the airport; northbound each ring ramp takes the right lane, 2 on to the signal. Ring lanes: ahead of the exits on each side an auxiliary lane opens; the local exit leaves it and the airport exit takes it, so the 3 ring lanes run unbroken. On the entry side the airport ramp and the local ramp join the ring side by side as a 2-lane entrance: the local lane runs 300 m and merges into the airport lane over a 150 m taper; the airport lane runs on as an added lane for 457 m (1,500 ft) and merges into the ring over a 150 m taper. Local traffic uses one signal on the local road 29 m north of the ring: ring west to the local side and the local side to ring east are left turns through it; ring east to the local side and the local side to ring west are free right slips onto and off the local road north of it. Southbound the local road adds its second lane, a left-turn bay and a right-turn bay before the signal. Hairpins 30 km/h (radius 31 to 34 m), slips 20 m, 7% at most, 6.1 m clear at every crossing.
